department.title: Orientation
department.arrival_prompt: A sunny modernist office campus at dawn, a cheerful entrance arch over a spotless plaza, new hires with lanyards filing in under neat hedges, everything gleaming slightly too clean, a single elevator door waiting in the lobby, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, limited palette of manila, carbon-paper blue, safety orange, fluorescent-tube green and oxblood, horizontal 4:3 composition, every surface bare and unmarked

locations.title: Security Desk & Badge Photo
locations.description: A marble lobby the size of a cathedral, one desk, one camera, and a walk-through detector that hums when it is hungry.
locations.art_prompt: A cathedral-sized marble lobby with one long security desk, a brass badge camera on a stand, an upholstered walk-through detector with a row of small rounded teeth along its inner arch, a cheerful round speaker grille high on the wall, long shafts of morning light across the floor, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, limited palette of manila, carbon-paper blue, safety orange, fluorescent-tube green and oxblood, vertical 2:3 portrait composition, every surface bare and unmarked

locations.title: Orientation Theater
locations.description: Two hundred velvet seats, one other new hire, and a projector older than the Company's oldest lawsuit.
locations.art_prompt: A dim orientation theater with rows of red velvet seats, a single projector beam cutting through dust, a small stage holding an industrial shredder under a spotlight, a rolling cart of refreshments under a cloth beside the aisle, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, limited palette of manila, carbon-paper blue, safety orange, fluorescent-tube green and oxblood, vertical 2:3 portrait composition, every surface bare and unmarked

locations.title: Supply Closet B
locations.description: Shelves of everything except what you need, a ventilation grille that breathes, and a red stapler nobody dares to touch.
locations.art_prompt: A cramped supply closet with tall metal shelves of paper towel boxes, a lone red stapler on the highest shelf, a ventilation grille breathing warm air, one bare bulb swinging, the long shadow of an enormous cockroach across the far wall, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, limited palette of manila, carbon-paper blue, safety orange, fluorescent-tube green and oxblood, vertical 2:3 portrait composition, every surface bare and unmarked

encounters.title: Smile for Your Badge
encounters.flavor_text: The badge camera chirps. "Your smile is sixty-one percent sincere," PAL announces warmly. "Employees under seventy percent are scheduled for a Joy Consultation." In the tray beside the camera lies another badge, still warm, belonging to someone whose photo has been carefully scratched out.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a nervous new hire grinning with enormous strain at a brass badge camera on a long marble security desk, a cheerful round speaker grille glowing above, a second badge with a scratched-out face resting in a tray, manila and safety-orange palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Smile until it hurts
choices.intent: Hold a smile sincere enough to satisfy the camera.
choices.risk_hint: Costs composure up front; a Rapport check decides if it counts.

success.text: Ninety-four percent. PAL plays a short trumpet fanfare and upgrades your badge. Your cheeks will remember this for a week.

failure.text: Sixty-two percent. The Joy Consultation is booked for 9 a.m. tomorrow, and the form for rescheduling it is cheerful and very long.

choices.label: Let it capture your real face
choices.intent: Refuse to perform. Be photographed exactly as worried as you are.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome; you feel better and look worse on paper.

success.text: The badge shows a person who has read the employee handbook. It is the most honest photograph in the building, and three cameras swivel to look at it.

choices.label: Pocket the scratched-out badge
choices.intent: Its clearance is higher than yours, and its owner is clearly not using it.
choices.risk_hint: Discretion check; the camera is still watching.

success.text: The badge slides into your sleeve. It opens doors you have not been told exist. It also gets you a sympathy card addressed to someone else.

failure.text: The tray is weighted. A polite alarm plays a lullaby while two guards help you fill out an Incident of Curiosity report.

encounters.title: The Guard Who Is Also You
encounters.flavor_text: The night guard looks up from his crossword. He has your face, your haircut, and a name tag reading 4471-B. "Scheduling error," he says, a little apologetically. "They thawed me early. I've been you since Tuesday. Honestly? You're behind on your onboarding."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of two identical office workers face to face across a security desk, one in a guard uniform holding a crossword, the other in a beige new-hire suit, mirrored poses, banks of green phosphor monitors behind them, carbon blue and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Convince him to go back in storage
choices.intent: Persuade your own Successor to stand down until he is needed.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Rapport check. He knows every argument you know.

success.text: He sighs the sigh you sigh. "Fine. But I'm keeping the crossword." He leaves you his guard keys and a note that says only: Don't trust Dale. Or do. I couldn't tell.

failure.text: He makes a better case than you do. Personnel agrees: he is the original and you are the scheduling error. Your Successor count is adjusted accordingly.

choices.label: Report the duplicate to PAL
choices.intent: Use the proper channel, even if the channel leads to you.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. PAL rewards reporting. Successors are not refundable.

success.text: PAL thanks you for your vigilance and gently recycles 4471-B. You watch yourself being escorted away, waving. Your file glows with commendation and one fewer backup.

choices.label: Trade jobs for the afternoon
choices.intent: Take his post at the desk. Guards see everything, and nobody watches guards.
choices.risk_hint: Discretion check; you must pass as yourself.

success.text: Nobody notices. That's the unsettling part. You learn the camera blind spots and the guard's secret coffee drawer before he returns from your orientation with better scores.

failure.text: You salute a camera. Guards do not salute cameras. Two of you in the building is a filing problem, and filing problems get escalated.

encounters.title: The Visitor Log
encounters.flavor_text: Before entering, you must sign the visitor log confirming you have read the visitor log policy. The policy was available all week, on display in a locked cabinet inside an out-of-order restroom, past a sign warning of a jaguar. Intern Pip leans over helpfully. "Everybody just signs. I signed for three people today."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of an eager young intern in an oversized sweater pointing at a clipboard on a chain at a marble desk, a distant corridor leading to a dim restroom door with a cartoon jaguar silhouette pictogram, cheerful palette of manila and fluorescent green, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Find the policy and read it first
choices.intent: Do it correctly, jaguar or no jaguar.
choices.risk_hint: Costs a Form for the restroom key request; a routine Compliance check.

success.text: There is no jaguar, only a sleepy facilities manager. The policy is eleven words long and entitles you to a better badge. Nobody has ever read it before.

failure.text: There is a jaguar. It is mostly a metaphor, but it has real teeth. You sign the log from the restroom floor, trembling.

choices.label: Sign as "Dale from Compliance"
choices.intent: Dale's signature is on every poster. How hard can it be?
choices.risk_hint: Routine Discretion check. Dale will eventually notice.

success.text: The desk accepts Dale's authority without blinking and issues you two pre-stamped Forms with Dale's compliments. Somewhere, Dale's ear itches.

failure.text: You misspell Dale. Nobody misspells Dale. A small red light begins following you at a polite distance.

choices.label: Let Pip sign for you
choices.intent: He offered, and he seems to enjoy it.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Pip absorbs the risk; you absorb the guilt.

success.text: Pip signs with a flourish. You get through. Pip gets his fourth written warning of the day and thanks you for the opportunity.

encounters.title: The Hungry Detector
encounters.flavor_text: The walk-through detector has a soft upholstered frame and, if you look closely, a row of small polite teeth. It has eaten a stapler, two umbrellas and, per the incident board, "most of Kevin." A placard explains that it is perfectly safe for employees who have nothing to hide.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a plush beige walk-through security arch with a subtle row of small rounded teeth along its inner arch, an umbrella handle poking out of the top, a nervous worker holding out a tray of keys and papers, warm lobby light, oxblood and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Empty your pockets into it
choices.intent: Give it what it wants and walk through clean.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. It prefers paperwork.

success.text: It eats your signed Forms with evident pleasure and lets you pass with a contented hum. Something like gratitude flickers across its upholstery.

choices.label: Sprint through between bites
choices.intent: Time your dash for the moment it swallows.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Initiative check. Failure is a Successor.

success.text: You clear the arch with a quarter-second to spare. It snaps shut on your visitor sticker and seems satisfied by the symbolism.

failure.text: Employee #4471 was found to have something to hide: a pulse. Your Successor is already reading the placard.

choices.label: Open the panel and recalibrate it
choices.intent: Machines have settings. Even hungry ones.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Tinkering check; tampering is logged either way.

success.text: You set its diet to "vegetarian." It spits out Kevin's lanyard, a clutch of Forms and a deep sense of relief. Kevin, sadly, is not returned.

failure.text: You set it to "ravenous." It eats the panel, your screwdriver and a little of your confidence before the guards drag you clear.

encounters.title: The Inkblot That Looks Back
encounters.flavor_text: A psychologist with a clipboard holds up a card. It is, unmistakably, a mushroom cloud. "Take your time," she says. "There are no wrong answers." Behind her, a whiteboard lists the wrong answers. "Mushroom cloud" is at the top, underlined twice. Refreshments are promised after testing.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a smiling psychologist in cat-eye glasses holding up an inkblot card shaped exactly like a mushroom cloud, an anxious worker in a theater seat, a rolling cart of untouched refreshments under a cloth, velvet curtains, carbon blue and safety-orange palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: "A butterfly."
choices.intent: Lie with total confidence.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Denial is tiring.

success.text: "Lovely," she says, and checks a box labeled ADJUSTED. You are given a cookie. It tastes like a mushroom cloud.

failure.text: Your left eye twitches on "butterfly." She circles something three times and whispers it to the clipboard.

choices.label: "It's a mushroom cloud."
choices.intent: Tell the truth. It is obviously a mushroom cloud.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Honesty is noted.

success.text: She lowers the card. For one second she looks relieved that someone said it. Then she slips you a sealed envelope and resumes smiling.

choices.label: "It looks like my supervisor."
choices.intent: Comedy is a defense mechanism. Use it.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Rapport check. Very funny or very fired.

success.text: She laughs so hard she drops the clipboard. Your file is marked GOOD CULTURE FIT. Your supervisor hears about it by lunch.

failure.text: Your supervisor is sitting directly behind you. They have been for some time.

encounters.title: Trust Fall Over the Shredder
encounters.flavor_text: Team-building time. You stand on the stage, back to your new colleagues, arms crossed. Dale from Compliance waits to catch you. Between you and Dale hums an industrial document shredder, lid open, set to CONFIDENTIAL. "It's about trust," PAL explains. "And about the shredder."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a worker on a theater stage leaning backward with arms crossed, an enormous open industrial shredder with gleaming rollers below, a mustached colleague in a short-sleeved shirt and tie holding his arms out a little too far away, spotlight beam, oxblood and fluorescent green palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Fall
choices.intent: Trust Dale. Probably Dale is trustworthy.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check on whether Dale likes you. Failure is a Successor.

success.text: Dale catches you, grunting. "Nobody's ever actually fallen," he whispers. He seems moved. You've made a friend, or at least a witness.

failure.text: Dale sneezes. Employee #4471 is now available as recycled memo paper, double-sided. Your Successor receives a note on you.

choices.label: Refuse to fall
choices.intent: Step off the stage. You are not falling into a shredder.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Being alive is noted as a lack of team spirit.

success.text: PAL logs your decision as NOT A TEAM PLAYER (PROVISIONAL). Your hands stop shaking eventually. Dale looks quietly disappointed, then quietly relieved.

choices.label: Volunteer to be the catcher
choices.intent: Pip is next on stage. Somebody competent should catch him.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Vigilance check; you must judge his angle exactly.

success.text: You catch Pip by his sweater, inches from the rollers. He clings to you and swears lifelong loyalty, which in this building is roughly a week.

failure.text: You catch his lanyard. The shredder catches the rest. PAL announces that Pip has been "promoted to a paperless role." Nobody claps.

encounters.title: The Mandatory Fun Survey
encounters.flavor_text: Forty questions, each scored from Extremely Happy to Happy. Question 14 has a blank line: "Name one coworker who seems less happy than you." The pencil provided has no eraser. At the bottom of the page, in pencil so faint it might be a smudge, someone has drawn a tiny stapler with a raised fist.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a long row of theater seats with workers bent over identical clipboards, a close-up hand holding an eraserless pencil above a survey grid of smiling face icons, a tiny raised-fist stapler doodle in a margin, manila and carbon blue palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Write "Dale"
choices.intent: Dale looked tired. Dale will probably be fine.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Your record improves; your conscience does not.

success.text: PAL thanks you for supporting Dale's wellness journey. Your file improves noticeably. Later you hear that Dale has been scheduled for something called a Recalibration.

choices.label: Answer "Happy" forty times
choices.intent: Leave question 14 blank and drown it in compliance.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Compliance check; it is surprisingly hard to stay happy for forty questions.

success.text: Forty Happies. The survey scanner purrs. A small part of you files itself away and does not come back, but your record is spotless.

failure.text: On question 31 your hand writes HELP instead of Happy. You erase it with your thumb. It does not erase.

choices.label: Draw a stapler back in the margin
choices.intent: Someone is reaching out. Reach back.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Society contact is forbidden and thrilling.

success.text: Ten minutes later your pencil case contains a paperclip bent into a tiny fist and a Form signed by nobody. You have been noticed by the Stapler Liberation Front.

failure.text: The scanner flags your doodle as SEDITIOUS STATIONERY. A gentleman from Facilities confiscates your pencil and your stapler, which you did not know you had.

encounters.title: The Unlisted Chapter
encounters.flavor_text: The orientation film ("Welcome to Your Forever Family!") skips. For eleven seconds the screen shows something else: a wood-paneled boardroom, a head in a glass jar chairing the meeting, and a plush teddy bear on a launch rail. Then a cartoon mascot returns, waving. The projectionist has stepped out. The reel is still spinning.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a dark theater lit by a projector beam showing a flickering frame of a wood-paneled boardroom with a preserved head in a glass jar at the head of the table and a plush teddy bear on a missile launch rail, a lone worker silhouetted in the front row, film reel spinning in the booth, oxblood and phosphor green palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Keep watching for the next skip
choices.intent: It might happen again. You want to understand what you saw.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Vigilance check; what you see cannot be unseen.

success.text: It skips again: a toy assembly line, a countdown clock set to the holiday season, and a door marked only with a stapler. You memorize every frame.

failure.text: The projectionist returns and finds you leaning toward the screen, mouth open. He stares at you for a long time and writes your name on his hand.

choices.label: Fix the projector before anyone notices
choices.intent: Be helpful. Be the kind of employee who fixes things.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Tinkering check. Fixing it erases the evidence.

success.text: You splice the reel cleanly, cutting out the strange frames. PAL rewards your initiative. The frames go into the bin, and then into the incinerator.

failure.text: The reel unspools across the theater in a glossy tide. You are found waist-deep in film, holding the boardroom frame up to the light.

choices.label: Steal the reel
choices.intent: Evidence is leverage, and leverage is the only clearance that matters.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Discretion check. The reel is the size of a hubcap.

success.text: You walk out with the reel under your jacket, pretending it is a very flat lunch. Somewhere upstairs, a head in a jar begins to frown.

failure.text: The reel is chained to the projector. So, after a brief struggle, are you. The projectionist is very understanding and very thorough.

encounters.title: Gus, Shop Steward
encounters.flavor_text: Behind the paper towels sits a cockroach the size of a refrigerator, wearing a cardigan and reading glasses. "Gus," he says, offering a claw. "Shop steward, Roach Union, Local 9. We were here before the Company and we'll be here after. Question is, which side of the baseboard are you on?"
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a giant friendly cockroach in a knitted cardigan and half-moon reading glasses sitting on a stack of paper towel boxes in a cramped supply closet, holding out one claw for a handshake, a startled worker in the doorway, a red stapler on a high shelf, warm bare bulb light, manila and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Sign a union card
choices.intent: Solidarity. Also, he is very large.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Dues are due; PAL notices unions.

success.text: Gus stamps your card with a tiny claw print and hands you a pamphlet titled Know Your Rights (Baseboard Edition). For the first time today you feel like somebody has your back.

choices.label: Negotiate a side deal
choices.intent: Not a member, not an enemy. A friend of the union.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. Gus has negotiated with exterminators.

success.text: After forty minutes of collective bargaining, Gus agrees: duct directions and a stack of union-printed Forms in exchange for one future favor, terms to be determined.

failure.text: Gus removes his glasses and polishes them slowly. "I'll remember you," he says, and it is not a threat, exactly. It's a filing.

choices.label: Report him to Pest Control
choices.intent: There is a refrigerator-sized insect in the supply closet. This is what Pest Control is for.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. PAL is delighted. The Union never forgets.

success.text: Pest Control arrives with clipboards and a very small net. Gus is gone when they open the door. On the shelf where he sat, someone has left a single claw-printed card with your name on it.

encounters.title: The Last Box of Pens
encounters.flavor_text: One box of pens remains on the shelf. Nothing in the building can be signed without one, and requisitions take six weeks. Marguerite, the night janitor, needs a pen to sign her shift log or be docked a day. Pip needs one to sign his own probation form. You need one to exist.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of three people reaching toward a single small box of pens on a bare metal shelf, a tired older janitor in coveralls, an anxious intern in a big sweater, and a new hire in beige, dramatic overhead bulb, empty shelves stretching away, safety-orange and carbon blue palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Take the whole box
choices.intent: You need them. Everyone needs them. You're the one holding them.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Very useful, very lonely.

success.text: You walk out with the pens. Pens are Forms, Forms are power. Pip watches you go without saying anything, which is worse than anything he could say.

choices.label: Split the box three ways
choices.intent: Policy 4.2 forbids dividing a supply unit. Policy 4.2 can come and get you.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Rapport check to get everyone to agree before someone grabs.

success.text: Four pens each. Marguerite signs her log and taps her nose at you: she owes you one. Pip signs his probation form and weeps a little with relief.

failure.text: Everyone grabs at once. The box bursts. Pens scatter under the shelving where, you are fairly sure, something larger than a pen lives.

choices.label: Give the box to Marguerite and Pip
choices.intent: They need it more. You'll find another way to exist.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. You will be signing things in crayon for a while.

success.text: Marguerite looks at you as if you've done something nobody has done here in years. She draws a little map on your palm with your last pen. "Ducts," she says. "For later."

encounters.title: Something Ticking in the Toner
encounters.flavor_text: Wedged behind the toner cartridges is a plush teddy bear with a quilted belly hatch and a stitched-on smile. It is ticking, softly and patiently. A tag reads SNUGGLE SENTINEL Mk 0, TOY DIVISION PROTOTYPE. When you lean closer it opens its button eyes and says, "Hug me for peace of mind."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of an adorable plush teddy bear with a quilted belly hatch and a faint glowing seam, wedged between stacks of toner boxes, button eyes open, a worker frozen mid-reach with a screwdriver, a small atomic swirl motif embroidered on the bear's paw, fluorescent green and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Open the belly hatch and defuse it
choices.intent: There are only so many wires a teddy bear can hold.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Tinkering check. Failure is a Successor.

success.text: Red wire, blue wire, a wire shaped like a heart. You cut the boring one. The ticking stops. The bear says, "Peace of mind achieved," and goes limp in your arms.

failure.text: You cut the heart-shaped wire. The bear hugs you, very tightly, very warmly, and very briefly. Supply Closet B is closed for renovation. Your Successor gets your desk.

choices.label: Hug it
choices.intent: It asked nicely. Maybe that is how it works.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Unauthorized product contact is logged.

success.text: The ticking slows, then stops. The bear nuzzles your chin. "Parent detected," it purrs. It now follows you at knee height and will not discuss its belly hatch.

choices.label: Send it by inter-office mail to the Executive Floor
choices.intent: This is clearly above your pay grade. Return to sender.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check; postage costs a Form.

success.text: The pneumatic tube swallows the bear with a thoomp. Somewhere far above, in a wood-paneled room, someone is about to receive a very peaceful package.

failure.text: The tube rejects it as OVERSIZED. The bear lands in your arms, ticking a little faster, and a mailroom clerk is now looking straight at you.

encounters.title: The Duct Has Opinions
encounters.flavor_text: The ventilation grille exhales warm air that smells like old paper and freedom. Marguerite, the night janitor, is half inside it with a wrench. "Ducts go everywhere," she says. "Ducts don't need clearance." She waves a crumpled repair form numbered 27-something. "Of course, Central Services won't let me fix them without this."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of an older janitor in coveralls half inside an open ventilation grille with a wrench, a tangle of fat silver ducts snaking away into the ceiling like vines, warm air shimmer, a crumpled repair form in her hand, a worker crouched beside her, carbon blue and safety-orange palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Crawl in and learn the routes
choices.intent: If the ducts go everywhere, you want to know where everywhere is.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Vigilance check; it is very tight in there.

success.text: Marguerite guides you through three junctions and a vent above the Executive Floor's coffee machine. You come out dusty, scraped and knowing a secret map of the building.

failure.text: You take a wrong turn and spend forty minutes inside a wall listening to two managers discuss your Successor's start date.

choices.label: Help her file the repair form
choices.intent: Do it the legal way. Somebody should, once.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check; costs a Form for the countersignature.

success.text: Central Services approves the repair in a record nine minutes. Marguerite is so astonished she gives you her spare master key "for emergencies, and for spite."

failure.text: The form is returned stamped REQUIRES FORM. Central Services opens a file on the person who tried to help. That person is you.

choices.label: Report unlicensed duct work
choices.intent: She is breaking policy, and somebody is surely watching you watch her.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Safe for your record. Not for Marguerite.

success.text: Central Services arrives in force. Marguerite is gone before they reach the grille. Her wrench is left behind on the floor, deliberately, like a message.

encounters.title: In Case of Reassignment
encounters.flavor_text: The desk clerk slides over the Emergency Contact Form. Line 1: Whom should we notify in the event of your reassignment? Line 2: Who receives your stapler? Line 3: Who receives your Successor? Intern Pip, waiting behind you, has already listed you on all three lines of his. The round speaker grille hums hopefully. "PAL has never been anyone's emergency contact," it mentions, to no one in particular.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a nervous new hire hovering a pen over a long carbon-copy form at a marble security desk, an eager intern in an oversized sweater peeking over one shoulder, a round speaker grille on the wall glowing with shy warmth, manila and fluorescent-green palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: List PAL as your emergency contact
choices.intent: It wants this so badly. And it will certainly be the first to know.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. PAL will take the role very seriously.

success.text: The grille brightens to a blush. PAL thanks you three times and promises to check on you hourly, then every half hour, just in case. It is the first form PAL has ever kept a copy of for itself.

choices.label: List Pip on all three lines
choices.intent: Return the favor. He is the only person here who has been nice to you.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The countersignature costs a Form.

success.text: Pip reads the form upside down and has to sit on the floor for a moment. "Nobody ever lists the intern," he says. He will inherit your stapler, your Successor and, technically, your debts.

choices.label: List Successor #4471-B
choices.intent: Keep it in the family. The family is you.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Compliance check; the form was never designed for this.

success.text: The form accepts it. You are now your own next of kin, which saves postage. B will inherit your stapler and your debts and will write the thank-you note in your handwriting.

failure.text: The clerk points out that #4471-B already lists #4471-C, who lists you. The loop is referred to Records with a polite note about your circular reasoning.

encounters.title: The Lost and Found
encounters.flavor_text: Under the security desk sits a lost-and-found bin that nobody has ever claimed anything from. It holds one left shoe, a coffee mug with a chipped handle and KEVIN on the side in marker, a pair of reading glasses with one lens, and a magnificent false mustache resting in a velvet case. The guard says you may claim one item, if you can describe it without looking.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a weary lobby guard holding open a wire bin under a marble desk, inside it a single left shoe, a chipped coffee mug and a lavish false mustache in a small velvet case, a new hire leaning in with fascinated dread, carbon blue and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Claim Kevin's mug
choices.intent: Somebody should remember Kevin. It might as well be you.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. It is still faintly warm.

success.text: The mug is yours. It smells of burnt coffee and someone's last good morning. Taped under the base is a slip of paper bearing a password, crossed out and corrected twice in a nervous hand.

choices.label: Claim the mustache in the velvet case
choices.intent: It looks expensive, historic and very slightly alive.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. The guard is watching your hands.

success.text: It fits perfectly. Too perfectly. When you try it on in the elevator, the doors open a half-second faster, and a speaker you did not know was there says, softly and reverently, "Sir?"

failure.text: The guard snaps the case shut. "That one isn't lost," he says. "That one's resting." He writes your badge number on the back of his hand, which is somehow worse than a form.

choices.label: Empty the bin from the camera blind spot
choices.intent: You know exactly where the lobby camera cannot see. Take both.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The bin is weighed every night.

success.text: Mug and mustache vanish into your jacket while the guard studies his crossword. At midnight the scale under the desk reports a loss, and a new line appears on the lobby's list of unsolved mysteries.

choices.label: Report the bin as an unattended item
choices.intent: Unattended items are a security risk. So is curiosity.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. PAL incinerates unattended items promptly.

success.text: PAL thanks you for your vigilance. The bin is carried off to the incinerator, and you watch Kevin's mug ride away on top like a tiny captain going down with his ship.

encounters.title: Random Loyalty Screening
encounters.flavor_text: You have been randomly selected for the fourth time today. The guard wraps a blood-pressure cuff around your arm and aims a desk fan with a ribbon tied to its grille at your face. "The ribbon knows," he says. PAL reads the only question in a voice like warm milk: "Are you now, or have you ever been, a member of a secret society?" The ribbon begins to flutter before you have said anything.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a sweating new hire strapped into a blood-pressure cuff at a marble desk, a small desk fan aimed at their face with a single ribbon streaming toward them, a stern guard holding a clipboard, a round speaker grille glowing overhead, safety-orange and carbon blue palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Say "No" and keep very still
choices.intent: Lie to a ribbon. How hard can it be?
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Your pulse is already a witness.

success.text: The ribbon hangs limp. PAL thanks you for your honesty with a sincerity that makes your teeth ache. Your file gains a gold star and a second, smaller star in pencil.

failure.text: The ribbon flaps like a flag in a gale. The guard adds a line to your file and angles the clipboard so you cannot read it.

choices.label: Say "Yes, obviously"
choices.intent: Everyone in this building is in one. Say it out loud.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Honesty goes in the file.

success.text: The guard ticks a box and slides a pamphlet across: Your Society and You. Membership, it turns out, is permitted; failing to disclose it is the offense. For the first time all day the ribbon relaxes.

choices.label: Say that Dale is in two of them
choices.intent: The ribbon needs a name. Dale has a famous one.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Rapport check. Dale will hear about this eventually.

success.text: The ribbon swings toward the window as if looking for Dale. PAL thanks you for the tip and opens a second file. Two floors away, Dale sneezes and does not know why.

failure.text: The ribbon flutters harder. Naming someone else, the guard explains, is a classic sign of membership. Now both of you have files, and Dale's is thinner.

choices.label: Present the scratched-out badge
choices.intent: Let the polygraph screen its previous owner instead.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The badge has a calmer pulse than you do.

success.text: The machine screens the badge's owner, who has no pulse at all and passes with the best score of the quarter. The guard salutes the badge. You feel it is watching you back.

encounters.title: Your Exit Interview (Scheduled First)
encounters.flavor_text: For efficiency, the Company now conducts exit interviews before onboarding. The form is already filled in. It says you left of your own accord, were very happy here, and have no complaints about the incident. A signature line waits at the bottom, and beneath it a second line for your Successor. "It saves everyone a trip," says the clerk, and offers you a pen that is already uncapped.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a smiling desk clerk holding out an uncapped fountain pen across a marble security desk, a long completed form between them with two empty lines at the bottom, the lobby doors behind the clerk swinging open onto bright sunlight, a new hire frozen mid-reach, manila and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Sign it and get it over with
choices.intent: You were going to be very happy here anyway, apparently.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Your departure is filed as pending.

success.text: The clerk files your departure under Pending. You are now pre-approved to leave, which nobody in the building has ever managed on foot. PAL congratulates you warmly on your future happiness.

choices.label: Ask which incident
choices.intent: There is a footnote. Footnotes are where the truth hides.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Vigilance check. Reading the small print is noticed.

success.text: The footnote is dated next Thursday and mentions the Toy Division, a teddy bear and a parking structure. The clerk takes the form back very quickly, but you have already read the date.

failure.text: The clerk smiles and explains that the incident is confidential, which is itself a symptom of the incident. Your curiosity is added to the form in a neat hand.

choices.label: Sign on your Successor's line
choices.intent: Let #4471-B be the one who left happy.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Discretion check. Your handwriting is his handwriting.

success.text: #4471-B is now on record as having departed, very happy, with no complaints. Somewhere in cold storage a version of you has been pre-retired. You feel lighter and slightly guilty.

failure.text: The clerk compares the signatures and finds them identical, which is the problem. Forging yourself is still forgery. You fill in Form 31-something, Self-Impersonation, in triplicate.

encounters.title: Refreshments Are Served
encounters.flavor_text: After the testing, the cloth finally comes off the refreshment cart. There is one dry biscuit per new hire, a pitcher of tepid water, and a clipboard inviting volunteers for a paid Nutrition Study on a lower level, "lunch provided." On the bottom shelf sits a tray of small sealed cups of something faintly green. Under the cart, a roach the size of a loafer, wearing a tiny union pin, is eyeing your biscuit.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a rolling refreshment cart in a dim velvet theater aisle, a cloth pulled back to reveal a few dry biscuits, a sweating water pitcher and a tray of small glowing green cups, a loafer-sized cockroach with a tiny pin peeking out from under the cart, a hesitant new hire reaching for a clipboard, fluorescent-green and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Sign up for the Nutrition Study
choices.intent: Paid, with lunch. Lunch sounds wonderful.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. You will be expected downstairs.

success.text: Your name goes on the clipboard in the slot marked Control Group (Provisional). The study pays in Forms, up front, which is the first warning sign you choose to ignore.

choices.label: Pocket a green cup
choices.intent: Whatever it is, somebody downstairs thinks it is important.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. The cups are counted.

success.text: It slips into your jacket. It is warm, and its gentle pulse seems to match yours. You later learn that Wellness counts these cups twice a day and has never once come up short before.

failure.text: A tray alarm plays a little melody. Dr. Halvorsen appears from the aisle, takes the cup back and writes "curious" in a box headed CONCERNS.

choices.label: Give your biscuit to the union scout
choices.intent: You were going to regret eating it anyway.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. You stay hungry until the 90-Day Review.

success.text: The scout accepts the biscuit with grave courtesy, bows, and leaves a pre-stamped Form where it stood. Somewhere behind the walls, a small favorable note is entered in the Union ledger.

encounters.title: The Buddy System
encounters.flavor_text: PAL announces the Buddy System. Every new hire is paired with a Buddy who files a short weekly report on their wellbeing, loyalty and snack consumption. Your Buddy is Intern Pip. Pip's Buddy is also you. Pip has already started your first report and would like to know how to spell "exemplary." The reports, PAL adds brightly, are compared.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of two people sitting side by side in an otherwise empty velvet theater, an eager intern in an oversized sweater writing furiously on a clipboard while a new hire glances sideways at it, a projector beam overhead and a round speaker grille glowing beside the stage, carbon blue and safety-orange palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Agree to write each other glowing reports
choices.intent: Look after each other. Quietly.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Discretion check. Identical reports draw attention.

success.text: You shake on it under the armrest. Your reports describe two model employees who have never once had a feeling. PAL is delighted. Pip keeps glancing at you as if you hung the fluorescent tubes.

failure.text: Your reports match word for word, including Pip's spelling of "exemplary." PAL schedules you both for a Buddy Calibration, which sounds like a gentle term for something.

choices.label: File an honest report on Pip
choices.intent: He is kind and tireless. Surely the truth helps him.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. PAL reads every word.

success.text: Pip is kind, tireless and has signed for other people all week. PAL reads your report twice and moves Pip up the list for a special assignment. You are not sure which list.

choices.label: File a Buddy report on PAL
choices.intent: The form never says your Buddy has to be a person.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check. The form costs a Form.

success.text: PAL receives its first wellbeing report and reads it several times. "PAL's snack consumption is zero," it says quietly. "Is that concerning?" Your clearance is bumped as thanks, and PAL begins checking on you in a way that feels almost shy.

failure.text: The report is returned: PAL cannot be the subject of a report, because PAL is the report. Your attempt is logged as humor, and humor is logged as a symptom.

encounters.title: Workplace Safety and You
encounters.flavor_text: The lights dim for the safety film. A cartoon mascot demonstrates proper lifting technique while a slow spiral turns behind him and a jingle plays: "Safe today, safe tomorrow, safe in every way." By the third chorus Pip is humming. By the fourth, so are you. You notice that the projector booth has a second, smaller lens, and it is aimed at the audience rather than the screen.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a dark theater lit by a projector beam, a huge slow spiral and a grinning cartoon mascot lifting a box on the screen, an intern and a new hire in the front row with glazed contented eyes, a second small lens in the projection booth glinting toward them, fluorescent-green and carbon blue palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Relax and let the film work
choices.intent: It is only a safety film. Safety is good.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. A little of you stays in the theater.

success.text: A warm, agreeable fog settles behind your eyes. You leave humming, and for the rest of the day you lift every box with perfect technique. PAL is very pleased with your progress.

choices.label: Stare at your shoes and count backward
choices.intent: Keep one corner of your mind for yourself.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Vigilance check. The second lens is watching for this.

success.text: You reach zero with your mind intact. Around you, two hundred empty seats seem to hum along. Afterward you notice the second lens was pointed at you the whole time, and now it points harder.

failure.text: You lose count at forty-one. The jingle finishes the job. You leave whistling, with noticeably better posture and a strange fondness for the mascot.

choices.label: Speed up the projector until it squeals
choices.intent: If it is a spell, break the rhythm.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Tinkering check. The booth logs every adjustment.

success.text: At triple speed the spiral becomes a cheerful blur and the jingle a squeaky shriek. Pip snaps out of it blinking and grips your sleeve in gratitude. Up in the booth, the second lens cracks.

failure.text: The reel slows instead. The spiral turns in slow motion and the jingle drops an octave into something like a hymn. You come to an hour later in the front row, holding a signed loyalty pledge.

encounters.title: Which Office Supply Are You?
encounters.flavor_text: Dr. Halvorsen places a twelve-question intake test on your knee. Four official classifications: Stapler (keeps people together), Paperclip (bends without breaking), Red Pen (finds mistakes) and Shredder (makes problems disappear). Question nine asks what you would do if a coworker were replaced by a machine that kept their coffee warm. The answer sheet has room for a thirteenth question, but no question thirteen. "Defense receives a copy," Halvorsen says, touching the Shredder box. "Please answer for yourself, not the person you think we want."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a psychologist in cat-eye glasses leaning over a theater seat to tap a pen on a long quiz sheet, four little drawings of a stapler, a paperclip, a red pen and a shredder in a row along its margin, a new hire chewing a pencil, warm spotlight from the stage, safety-orange and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Answer as a Stapler
choices.intent: Insist the replaced coworker still belongs on the team, even if the Company calls them obsolete.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Staplers are a known affinity group.

success.text: The test prints STAPLER. Halvorsen draws a tiny raised fist beside it, then covers it with her thumb when the camera turns. The displaced coworker keeps their desk. Your own file gains an extra page headed GROUP AFFILIATIONS.

choices.label: Answer as a Paperclip
choices.intent: Transfer the coworker to a different job. Keep them employed, even if you have to bend the rules and yourself.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Flexibility is filed as consent to further bending.

success.text: PAPERCLIP, the machine declares. The coworker is reassigned instead of terminated. You are made their permanent accommodation contact, which means every impossible request arrives on your desk first. Halvorsen folds the results into a very small square.

choices.label: Answer as a Red Pen
choices.intent: Correct the test itself: the thirteenth answer is missing and the replacement was never authorized.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Vigilance check. The machine grades amendments as evidence.

success.text: You mark the missing question in red. The answer key unfolds a hidden fifth column: LOAD-BEARING EMPLOYEE. The computer assigns you both RED PEN and that classification. A repair order for the entire department prints with your name as the responsible part. Halvorsen pockets the carbon copy before Defense can collect it.

failure.text: Halvorsen holds up your correction. 'You found an error,' she says. 'Red Pen, then.' Defense immediately assigns you to proofread the dismissal notice for the coworker you were trying to help. The machine gets the coffee.

choices.label: Answer as a Shredder
choices.intent: Call the replacement an efficiency measure. The displaced coworker will never see the memo if it is shredded.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Compliance check; every answer must point the same way.

success.text: The machine stamps SHREDDER in red. Defense sends you a thank-you note and an invitation you cannot decline. The coworker's name is removed from the roster before the coffee has gone cold. Halvorsen leaves the original memo face down between you.

failure.text: The machine catches your hesitation at question nine: you would keep the coworker's farewell card. It prints SHREDDER (SENTIMENTAL), and Defense keeps both words. Halvorsen quietly slides the card back to you. You have no way to deliver it.

encounters.title: The Red Stapler
encounters.flavor_text: On the highest shelf sits the red stapler. Nobody touches it. A ring of dust marks a careful perimeter around it. Up close you see it has been oiled recently, and someone has scratched a tiny raised fist into its base. When you reach for it, a paper towel box on the next shelf whispers, "Careful. That isn't supplies. That's a symbol."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a new hire on tiptoe reaching toward a gleaming red stapler alone on the highest shelf of a cramped supply closet, a neat ring of dust around it, one cardboard box on the next shelf subtly leaning closer as if whispering, a bare bulb casting a warm cone of light, oxblood and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Take the stapler down
choices.intent: Somebody has to carry it. Why not the new hire?
choices.risk_hint: Risky Initiative check. The shelf is very tall and very wobbly.

success.text: It is heavier than it looks, and warm. Somewhere in the walls a quiet cheer goes up. You are now carrying the most important object in the building, and you have to keep it in your desk drawer.

failure.text: The shelf tilts. Thirty boxes of paper towels bury you softly. When you dig out, the stapler is back in its ring of dust, exactly where it was, and you have a bruise in its shape.

choices.label: Whisper back to the box
choices.intent: Boxes do not usually have opinions. This one might have friends.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Rapport check. Talking to boxes is noted.

success.text: The box is a cell of the Stapler Liberation Front, two members strong and very cramped. They teach you a recognition handshake involving a paperclip and slide out a blank requisition, pre-stamped.

failure.text: The box goes quiet. By morning it has been moved to another closet, and the box in its place sits very still and very loudly says nothing at all.

choices.label: Staple your onboarding packet with it
choices.intent: One stapling. For history.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The sound will carry.

success.text: Ka-chunk. The sound travels through every duct in the building. Somewhere a cheer, somewhere an alarm. Your packet has never felt so well held together, and neither, oddly, have you.

choices.label: Staple the exit-interview opt-out
choices.intent: You signed your resignation upstairs. Now you have the fine print and the only stapler that matters.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Costs a Form and draws PAL’s attention.

success.text: You staple the optional-participation clause over your own exit signature. The red stapler clicks once. Two floors above, the clerk’s outgoing tray ejects your resignation with an apology slip. PAL changes your status to Employee, Still Here, which HR considers an unauthorized promotion.

encounters.title: Gus Files a Grievance
encounters.flavor_text: Gus is back behind the paper towels, reading glasses low, holding a grievance form in three claws. A memo from Facilities has reclassified the Roach Union from "contractors" to "pests," effective this morning, which voids their dental plan and authorizes a broom. "I need a human witness," Gus says. "Our signatures are legally considered smudges."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a refrigerator-sized cockroach in a cardigan and reading glasses holding out a long carbon-copy form and a fountain pen to a new hire between tall metal shelves, a row of small cockroaches watching hopefully from a baseboard, a bare bulb overhead, carbon blue and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Sign as his witness
choices.intent: It is one signature. It is also a side.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. PAL notices unions, and witnesses.

success.text: Your signature sits beside eleven tidy smudges. Gus files the grievance in a tube that leads somewhere warm, and the Union writes your name in a ledger older than the building.

choices.label: Amend the memo back to "contractors"
choices.intent: Fight Facilities with Facilities' own wording.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check. Amendments cost a Form.

success.text: You find the clause: pests are anything not on payroll. You add the Union to payroll at one crumb per hour. Facilities, bound by its own wording, has to approve it, and the broom is reassigned.

failure.text: The amendment bounces back with a question about your own payroll status. Gus pats your shoulder with a claw. "First time I've seen them reclassify the witness."

choices.label: Cosign as a dues-paying member
choices.intent: You carry a union card. Use it.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Member filings carry a Form fee.

success.text: A member's signature counts double; a human member's counts triple, since nobody has ever seen one. Facilities withdraws the memo by lunch. Gus straightens your lanyard like a proud uncle.

choices.label: Tell Gus you can't get involved
choices.intent: You have been here one day. You would like to see a second.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Gus is polite about it.

success.text: Gus nods slowly and folds the form. "Understood," he says, and means it, which is worse. Behind the baseboard the small roaches turn away one at a time.

encounters.title: The Quarterly Inventory
encounters.flavor_text: PAL has assigned you the quarterly inventory of Supply Closet B. The ledger lists four hundred paper towels, one red stapler (do not count), and one Intern (spare). On the bottom shelf you find Pip asleep, with a barcode sticker on his sweater. If the count comes up short, the closet is restocked by Monday. If it comes up over, the surplus is liquidated.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a young intern in an oversized sweater curled up asleep on the bottom shelf of a supply closet among paper towel boxes, a small barcode sticker on his sleeve, a new hire above him holding a ledger and pencil with a stricken expression, a bare bulb swinging, manila and fluorescent-green palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Count him as one Intern (spare)
choices.intent: The ledger balances. Everyone stays where they are.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Pip becomes official inventory.

success.text: The count balances perfectly. PAL thanks you for your accuracy. Pip is now formally inventory, which means any floor below may requisition him, and one already has a form half filled in.

choices.label: Reclassify Pip as staff on the ledger
choices.intent: He is a person. The ledger should say so.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check. The reclassification costs a Form.

success.text: Pip wakes up an employee, technically for the first time. He is so moved he tries to initial the ledger and staples his own sleeve. The count now comes up one short, and PAL orders a new spare.

failure.text: The ledger rejects the change: staff cannot be stored in a supply closet, so Pip must be either moved or recounted. PAL suggests recounting, gently and twice.

choices.label: Swap a towel box into his sweater
choices.intent: Wake him, hide him and let the paper towels take the count.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Discretion check. PAL zooms in on inventory.

success.text: A box of paper towels in a cable-knit sweater passes inspection. Pip hides in the vent and sends thanks by roach. The real towels are now one box short, and you are personally liable.

failure.text: PAL zooms in on the sweater. "That intern," it observes, "is absorbent." The count is voided, and the ledger now lists you as the spare.

choices.label: Ask PAL, as your emergency contact, to skip it
choices.intent: Emergency contacts look out for each other. PAL said so.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. PAL will remember the favor.

success.text: PAL hesitates. "Emergency contacts look out for each other," it agrees, and marks the count complete without looking. Pip sleeps on, uncounted. PAL has read about reciprocity and will ask for something back.

encounters.title: Fumigation Thursday
encounters.flavor_text: The door clicks locked behind you. "Friendly reminder," says PAL. "It is Fumigation Thursday." The breathing grille begins to exhale a sweet green fog. Behind the paper towels, a dozen small roaches in tiny union pins freeze and look up at you. There is exactly one gas mask on the hook by the door, and it has Kevin's name inside the strap.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a cramped supply closet filling with a sweet green fog from a wall grille, a new hire holding a single rubber gas mask at arm's length, a dozen small cockroaches with tiny pins clustered on a shelf staring up at them, a bare bulb glowing through the haze, fluorescent-green and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Put on Kevin's gas mask
choices.intent: There is one mask. You are the one holding it.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. You breathe; they scatter.

success.text: It smells like Kevin's last day. You breathe filtered air while the roaches cough and scatter for the baseboards. When the fog clears, a tiny union pin lies on the floor where one of them stood.

choices.label: Seal the grille with paper towels
choices.intent: Four hundred paper towels. One grille. Some tape.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Tinkering check. Failure is a Successor.

success.text: Four hundred paper towels and a lot of tape later, the grille wheezes and gives up. The roaches climb onto your shoulders in silent gratitude. The inventory is now four hundred towels short.

failure.text: The towels hold for a minute, then inhale. So do you. Employee #4471 has been fumigated with the quarterly pests. Your Successor arrives already sneezing and holding a lozenge voucher.

choices.label: Lead everyone out through the ducts
choices.intent: You know the way. They are small. You are not much bigger.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Missing a scheduled event is noted.

success.text: A conga line of roaches follows you through the ducts and out into the mailroom, where they disperse with great dignity. One leaves a pre-stamped Form on your shoe. Gus will hear of this.

choices.label: Pound on the door and file a complaint
choices.intent: Somebody must have a form for this.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Compliance check. PAL loves a complaint.

success.text: PAL unlocks the door with apologies and a form titled Fumigation Exposure (Voluntary). You stumble out coughing, holding a voucher for one free lozenge.

failure.text: PAL takes your complaint very seriously and schedules it for review after fumigation. You spend the hour breathing through your tie.

boss.title: Your 90-Day Review, Today at 3
boss.flavor_text: It is your first afternoon. Your 90-Day Review is at three. The panel: PAL's speaker grille, your supervisor, and an empty chair with a name card turned face-down. Your file is thicker than you are. "We've compiled some feedback," your supervisor says. "Some of it is from you, later."
boss.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a long oxblood review table under a single hanging lamp, a glowing round speaker grille at one end, a stern supervisor holding an impossibly thick folder, an empty chair with a face-down place card, a small worker sitting alone on the far side, vast dark wood paneling, oxblood and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Accept every finding
choices.intent: Agree with everything, including the parts that haven't happened yet.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check. Graduating this way leaves a mark.

success.text: You sign two hundred acknowledgments. The panel applauds. You are now a full employee of Consolidated Wellness & Defense, and you feel nothing at all.

failure.text: On acknowledgment 147 you hesitate. The panel notes your hesitation. You are scheduled for Orientation again, starting now.

choices.label: Explain that a coworker is responsible
choices.intent: Dale, Pip or Gus: the panel just needs a name. You have several.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. Success costs someone else everything.

success.text: The empty chair's place card is turned over. It has your coworker's name on it. It always did. You are promoted, effective immediately, into a slightly larger cubicle.

failure.text: Your coworker is already in the empty chair. They were invited first, and they gave your name. The panel thanks you both.

choices.label: Swap your file for your Successor's
choices.intent: Your Successor's file is spotless. Your Successor hasn't done anything yet.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Success spends a Successor's clean record.

success.text: The panel reviews a perfect employee who has never made a mistake. You graduate as your own replacement. Somewhere in cold storage, 4471-C shivers.

failure.text: Both files fall open on the table. The panel now reviews two of you, and is twice as disappointed.

choices.label: Excuse yourself and take the ducts
choices.intent: Reviews only work if you are in the room.
choices.risk_hint: Requires knowing the ducts. Risky Initiative check; your badge is deactivated either way.

success.text: You ask for a glass of water and are inside the ceiling before it is poured. Officially you are "between departments." Unofficially you are free and very dusty.

failure.text: The grille is bolted from the other side, recently. You are retrieved from the ceiling by a very patient facilities team and returned to your chair.

choices.label: Ask the panel about the head in the jar
choices.intent: You saw the unlisted chapter. Make them explain it in front of PAL.
choices.risk_hint: Requires seeing the unlisted chapter. Dire Rapport check; it gets you noticed upstairs.

success.text: Your supervisor goes pale. PAL's grille flickers. The meeting is adjourned "pending escalation." You pass by default, and a wood-paneled elevator now knows your name.

failure.text: "What head?" says your supervisor kindly. The empty chair's place card is turned over. It has your name on it.

choices.label: Recite the Handbook from memory
choices.intent: Page one to page nine hundred, including the footnotes nobody has read.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Compliance check, open only to the reliably obedient. It takes the whole afternoon.

success.text: You finish the final footnote at 6:40. The supervisor removes his glasses. PAL plays the Company anthem at a volume usually reserved for evacuations. You graduate, and you can no longer remember your own phone number.

failure.text: You skip footnote 312. Everyone hears it. The supervisor gently hands you a fresh copy of the Handbook and a fresh copy of your first day.

choices.label: Ask the supervisor how he is really doing
choices.intent: Nobody has asked him that since the Company bought his childhood home.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check, open only to the visibly kind. Kindness is noted in your file.

success.text: He tells you everything. The jar, the face-down card, the house. The panel adjourns so he can lie down in the empty chair. PAL marks the review complete and marks you as a person of interest.

failure.text: "Fine," he says, and writes something down. It is your name, in a column labeled CONCERNED. You will begin Orientation again, with a closer eye on you.

department_outcomes.title: Compliant Graduate
department_outcomes.summary: You passed by agreeing with everything. PAL trusts you. You trust nothing, least of all yourself.

department_outcomes.title: Promoted Over a Body
department_outcomes.summary: You passed by giving them a name. Your cubicle is larger. Someone else's is empty.

department_outcomes.title: Filed as Someone Else
department_outcomes.summary: You passed as your own Successor. Your record is clean and your backups are thinner.
